summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.

key_cases.case_name: In re Child of Philip S.
key_cases.holding: The Law Court affirmed dismissal for lack of standing of a de facto parentage complaint brought by the paternal uncle and aunt after the child was removed from their kinship placement and placed with a non-kinship foster family.
key_cases.relevance: Kinship caregivers in Maine must satisfy every element of the de facto parentage standing statute, 19-A M.R.S. § 1891, by a preponderance before they get a plenary hearing.
key_cases.quote: The special standing requirement acknowledges that a parent defending against such litigation inherently suffers an intrusion on parental rights.

key_cases.holding: The Law Court affirmed denial of relief from a final termination judgment and denial of intervention and interested-person status to a cousin couple and to an unrelated couple, holding that kinship-placement claims never raised during the termination proceeding were waived and that intervention requires a demonstrated special relationship with the child.
key_cases.relevance: Relatives who wish to be considered for kinship placement under 22 M.R.S. § 4062(4) must come forward during the protective proceeding, not after termination.
key_cases.quote: A special relationship with the child must be demonstrated.

key_cases.holding: The Law Court affirmed appointment of the paternal grandparents as full guardians over the mother's objection, holding the Probate Court's findings that the mother was unfit and presented a temporarily intolerable living situation and that the appointment served the child's best interest satisfied 18-A M.R.S. §§ 5-204 and 5-207.
key_cases.relevance: It is the working model of a kinship guardianship established with one parent's consent and over the other parent's objection.
key_cases.quote: Here, there was no dispute as to venue or notice, and the court found all of the elements necessary to support a guardianship judgment pursuant to sections 5-204 and 5-207.

key_cases.holding: The Law Court vacated a temporary guardianship awarded to a grandmother, holding that the finding of a temporarily intolerable living situation was clearly erroneous because the overwhelming record evidence showed the mother was a fit parent at the time of the hearing.
key_cases.relevance: A relative caregiver cannot convert de facto care into legal custody without clear and convincing proof of the parent's current unfitness.
key_cases.quote: Given the overwhelming record evidence that Nicole was a fit parent at the time of the hearing, the court's finding to the contrary is clearly erroneous

key_cases.holding: The Law Court affirmed summary judgment for two Department caseworkers, holding that their decisions about how much of a child's sexual-abuse history to disclose to relatives seeking his placement were discretionary functions absolutely immune under 14 M.R.S.A. § 8111(1)(C), even assuming negligence or bad faith.
key_cases.relevance: The relatives who took the child in had no tort remedy when the caseworkers withheld his history, which is the practical risk kinship caregivers assume in Maine.
key_cases.quote: The Legislature has immunized from suit caseworkers' discretionary actions within the scope of their employment.

key_cases.case_name: Maureen D. Davis v. Bennie C. McGuire III
key_cases.holding: The Law Court affirmed dismissal of a grandmother's de facto parentage complaint for lack of standing, holding that a single standard of proof governs the standing determination under 19-A M.R.S. § 1891 — a burden of persuasion, not mere production — so that the petitioner must prove every statutory element of a de facto parent relationship by a preponderance of the evidence whether the court decides standing on the affidavits or after a hearing.
key_cases.relevance: This is the decision that established the standing burden In re Child of Philip S. applies to kinship caregivers: a relative must prove every element of 19-A M.R.S. § 1891(3) by a preponderance before any plenary de facto parentage hearing is available.
key_cases.quote: a petitioner must prove each of the elements of a de facto parent relationship with the child by—as we now hold—a preponderance of the evidence.
